## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
All scripts/codes required to reproduce all analyses reported in the paper and appendix are present in human-readable form and publicly available, preferably in a trusted repository with a persistent identifier (e.g. a DOI). If only raw data are included, the code to clean them into the analysis data must be included as well.

[Supported by: [#12](../../sources.qmd#p12 "Reproducibility: a primer on semantics and implications for research") code for all principal results in human-readable form + code from raw to analysis data, [#78](../../sources.qmd#p78 "CRRESS - session 4 - reproducibility and confidential data") extraction/scraping/cleaning/analysis code, [#109](../../sources.qmd#p109 "A protocol for structured robustness reproductions and replicability assessments") cleaning + analysis code as checklist items, [#131](../../sources.qmd#p131 "Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences") ACRE levels, [#141](../../sources.qmd#p141 "Understanding cultural persistence and change: A replication of Giuliano and Nunn (2021)") missing appendix code, [#93](../../sources.qmd#p93 "Unintended code errors and computational reproducibility") 'all files necessary', [#70](../../sources.qmd#p70 "The Stark realities of reproducible statistically orientated sociological research: Some newer rules of the sociological method"), [#20](../../sources.qmd#p20 "Successes and struggles with computational reproducibility: lessons from the fragile families challenge"), [#10](../../sources.qmd#p10 "Sustainable computational science: the ReScience initiative").]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
Code is available but incomplete: e.g. the cleaning code is missing although only raw data are shared, or the code for some results (e.g. appendix tables, robustness checks) is missing.

[Supported by: [#131](../../sources.qmd#p131 "Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences") L3/L6 (partial code), [#125](../../sources.qmd#p125 "A report on 'corruption and Co-optation in autocracy: evidence from Russia'") and [#100](../../sources.qmd#p100 "Computational and robustness reproducibility of 'UN peacekeeping and democratization in conflict-affected countries'") cleaning code 'Partial' vs. analysis code 'Fully', [#141](../../sources.qmd#p141 "Understanding cultural persistence and change: A replication of Giuliano and Nunn (2021)") code for the appendix missing.]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
No scripts/codes are available.

[Supported by: [#109](../../sources.qmd#p109 "A protocol for structured robustness reproductions and replicability assessments") 'not computationally reproducible if code is missing', [#86](../../sources.qmd#p86 "What makes computational communication science (ir)reproducible?") 'no shared code' = failure, [#98](../../sources.qmd#p98 "Mass reproducibility and replicability: a new hope") rating 1, [#131](../../sources.qmd#p131 "Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences") L1/L2, [#70](../../sources.qmd#p70 "The Stark realities of reproducible statistically orientated sociological research: Some newer rules of the sociological method").]{.source-note}
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never.
:::

**[#131](../../sources.qmd#p131)** Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences · *injunctive*

> Level 1 (L1): No data or code are available. Possible improvements include adding: raw data, analysis data, cleaning code, and analysis code. You may have detected papers without any reproduction materials at the Paper Selection stage, where you should have recorded them as abandoned candidate papers.
>
> Level 2 (L2): Code scripts are available (partial or complete), but no data are available. Possible improvements include adding: raw data and analysis data.
>
> Level 3 (L3): Analytic data and code are partially available, but raw data and cleaning code are missing. Possible improvements include: completing analysis data and/or code, adding raw data, and adding analysis code.
>
> Level 4 (L4): All analytic data sets and analysis code are available, but the code fails to run or produces results inconsistent with the paper (not CRA). Possible improvements include: debugging the analysis code or obtaining raw data.
>
> Level 5 (L5): Analytic data sets and analysis code are available and they produce the same results as presented in the paper (CRA). The reproducibility package may be improved by obtaining the original raw data.
>
> Note: This is the highest level that most published research papers can attain currently. Computational reproducibility from raw data is required for papers that are reproducible at Level 6 and above.
>
> Level 6 (L6): Cleaning code scripts are available (partial or complete), but raw data is missing. Possible improvements include: adding raw data.
>
> Level 7 (L7): Cleaning code is available and complete, and raw data is partially available. Possible improvements: adding raw data.
>
> Level 8 (L8): All the materials (raw data, analytic data, cleaning code, and analysis code) are available. However, the cleaning code fails to run or produces different results from those presented in the paper (not CRR) or the analysis code fails to run or produces results inconsistent with the paper (not CRA). Possible improvements: debugging the cleaning or analysis code.
>
> Level 9 (L9): All the materials (raw data, analytic data, cleaning code, and analysis code) are available. The analysis code produces the same output as presented in the paper (CRA). However, the cleaning code fails to run or produces different results from those presented in the paper (not CRR). Possible improvements: debugging the cleaning code.
>
> Level 10 (L10): All necessary materials are available and produce consistent results with those presented in the paper. The reproduction involves minimal effort and can be conducted starting from the analytic data ( CRA) and the raw data (CRR). Note that Level 10 is aspirational and may be unattainable for most research published today.
